hypotheses.statement: The brain learns to bond: in the last quarter of the run the policies' own probability of choosing bond (before innate priors) is higher in the cooperation arm than in the placebo, where it never pays.
Cooperation sustains a larger population than the same world without working units.
Cooperation lengthens lives: agents that die in the cooperation arm lived longer than in the placebo. Unlike population, lifespan has no ceiling when the population sits at its cap.
Selection acts on scope: the run-long change in the population mean of coop_scope differs from its neutral drift in the placebo.
Selection acts on exit_cost: the run-long change in the population mean of coop_exit_cost differs from its neutral drift in the placebo.
Selection acts on recognition: the run-long change in the population mean of coop_recognition differs from its neutral drift in the placebo.
Selection favours binding terms: the population mean of recognition x exit cost (the enforced exit payment per unit of the exit-cost base) rises more than under neutral drift.
Units form at all: coverage in the cooperation arm exceeds the placebo's, which is zero by construction.
The cost of carrying two extra actions and twelve extra loci without a working institution.
The brains learn at all: late in the run the policies' own probability of gather (before priors) exceeds uniform, in the unmodified world.
Learning shows in behaviour: the late gather share exceeds what the innate priors alone would give.
Selection acts on symmetry: the run-long change in the population mean of coop_symmetry differs from its neutral drift in the placebo.
Selection acts on exclusivity: the run-long change in the population mean of coop_exclusivity differs from its neutral drift in the placebo.
Selection acts on max_members: the run-long change in the population mean of coop_max_members differs from its neutral drift in the placebo.
Insurance works: fewer agents starve to death in the cooperation arm.
Cooperation raises turnover: more births over the run than in the placebo.
